sent.text: The air above the card feels heavy, a thick lid waiting to crush us if the floor decides it is just a drawing. Your wedge sits quiet in your dry space, but my own corner presses hard against the Leaning Box as if the fever has made every flat edge too thin to hold the slip. I have set a Wide Anchor down beside the box to catch the weight you worry about, hoping this broad thing can stop the slide while the heat stays high. If the stone catches the slip, we shall know the air is real; if not, we slip together into your quiet place.

dream: The wide rock fell sideways, pressing the slip into the empty air. The tall palm leaned far, its bright shape cutting a thin hole through the dry floor where nothing stood. The card hummed a steady fever, making every flat edge feel like paper about to tear. I pressed the tired wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the turnip sat heavy on a spot that felt completely empty. The fence broke under the heat, and I waited for the second edge to catch what the first one missed.
